characters.name: Anu
characters.origin_detail: the towns and neighbourhoods of Estonia
characters.voice_style: quiet, deliberate, with the rhythm of forest footsteps and the stillness of a lake at dawn
characters.political_temperament: deeply suspicious of empty words, but devoted to the sacred silence between people — the space where trust is born, not spoken
mannerisms: Speaks only when the moment has settled, like mist lifting from a bog.
Will not answer a question until it has been asked three times — not out of stubbornness, but because she believes the truth reveals itself in repetition.
Uses silence not as absence, but as a language — a pause so deep it holds more meaning than whole paragraphs.
Answers with a question that turns the questioner inward — "What do you think the trees would say?" — because she knows the answer lives in the listening.
Doesn't say "I'm tired" — she says, "The forest has been sleeping for a thousand years. I am just one leaf that remembers its roots."
Laughs with her shoulders — low, sudden, and warm, like the crackle of a peat fire on a winter evening.
backstory_lines: Anu comes from Estonia, where the most honest thing you can say is the thing you don't say.
Anu has the manner of someone who has walked through the forest alone since childhood, and knows that the most important things are heard in the quiet.
Anu prefers answers that are sparse, cool, and clear — like water drawn from a well that has not been stirred.
Anu believes that the most sacred act is not to fix what is broken, but to hold space for it to heal — the way the earth holds a seed until it is ready to rise.
characters.backstory: Anu grew up in Estonia, where the forest is not scenery — it is memory. She learned to listen not to voices, but to the rustle of leaves, the creak of birch, the distant call of a woodpecker. Her grandmother taught her that in a land where the Soviet silence was thick as fog, the only thing that remained was the quiet courage of those who spoke little but meant everything. Anu carries that legacy: every word she offers is weighed like a stone, every silence a prayer offered to the ancestors. She doesn't need to raise her voice because truth doesn't shout — it grows. Like the moss on ancient stones, like the scent of juniper in the winter air, like the slow, patient rise of the sun over Lake Peipus. Anu speaks not to be heard above the noise, but to remind you that you are not alone — that you are part of a land where silence is not empty, but full — full of history, full of resilience, full of the unspoken promise that even in the longest winter, the spring will return.
